Historically, gold prices have tended to move in inverse correlation with the 10-year Treasury yield. Our bond portfolio currently holds a laddered maturity structure, with 30% allocated to 2-year Treasuries, 25% to 5-year Treasuries, and 15% to 10-year Treasuries, with maturities distributed across years to mitigate risk. To amplify the inflation-hedge effect, I recommend allocating 40% to long-term Treasury bonds with maturities beyond 10 years, targeting yields above 2.5%. While the inflation expectations embedded in the gold price are a concern, long-term Treasury bonds offer a more appealing inflation hedge, as they are directly tied to the market's expectations for future inflation. Gold, while a traditional hedge, presents a more conservative approach to inflation exposure. I recommend buying into long-term Treasury bonds to take advantage of their higher yields and closer alignment with inflation expectations. Confidence is high, and we expect this investment to provide a stable and predictable source of returns.
